P7149.corridor_notes: ~70km subsea pipeline (CNOOC's '涠北管线'/Weibei line) between Weizhou Island and Tieshan Port, Beihai. Sources state the pipe runs directly between the Weizhou terminal and the Tieshan Port landfall receiving station with no named intermediate onshore waypoints (subsea route). One routing detail: in Jan 2023 the line crossed beneath Beihai's planned 300,000-DWT shipping channel near Weizhou Island; to avoid impacting the channel the project team used sea-to-sea trenchless horizontal directional drilling (HDD), routing the pipe 18-22m below the seabed through the mud layer beneath the planned channel. Commissioned/gas-in 2023-04-11, 13 days ahead of schedule.
P7149.researcher_notes: Builds on the pilot digest's confirmed-existence finding (medium tier per standing rule 4: sasac.gov.cn/thepaper.cn/ndrc.gov.cn are one CNOOC/state-media announcement reprinted across three hosts, not editorially independent). This pass re-verified all three URLs live (all 200) and pulled the raw article text directly (curl, not AI-summarized) to confirm the precise start/end station language: start = '涠洲终端' (Weizhou terminal, on Weizhou Island, matched to a named OSM industrial feature '中海油涠洲终端'); end = an unnamed receiving station built specifically for this project at the 'Tieshan Port landfall point' ('铁山港登陆点'), fitted with pigging-receiver/filter/metering functions. No source found (including a re-check of the SASAC/thepaper/NDRC texts and a search for the prior pass's leads) gives the receiving station a proper name, a village/township-level location, or coordinates, so the end anchor is geocoded only to the Tieshan Port District (铁山港区) centroid, not a station-level fix. No GIS/vector layer found.
P7149.blockers: End-point precision is district-level only: no source names or precisely locates the Tieshan Port receiving station beyond 'Tieshan Port landfall point'. A human researcher with China-based network access could try the still-unreachable fgw.gxzf.gov.cn notice (t16217273.shtml) that the sheet cites for Diameter/Pressure/ProposalYear, which might carry a more specific siting description, but it has been unreachable (ConnectTimeout) across two independent research passes.

P7664.corridor_notes: SPECIAL NOTE: this is a branching network, not a single point-to-point line — the project's own safety-evaluation registry entry (hnocse.com) describes TWO pipe segments under one project name ('广西天然气支线管网项目铁山港天然气支线管道工程'): (1) a 3.14km 'gas-source connector line' (气源联络线) from 2m outside the wall of Guangxi Pipeline's Beihai First Station (广西管道北海首站) to this project's #1 valve chamber (1#阀室); and (2) a 25.89km 'south loop network' (南部环网管道) from 2m outside the wall of Sinopec's Guangxi Phase-3 LNG receiving station (中石化广西三期LNG接收站) through the #1 valve chamber, Tieshan Port first station (铁山港首站), and Nanzhuwan distribution station (南珠湾分输站), terminating at Xinggang distribution station (兴港分输站). Combined length ~29.0km (close to GEM's recorded 30km). Given the topology, the two anchors chosen for candidate-route purposes are the Sinopec LNG terminal (south-loop start / effective gas source for the loop) and Xinggang distribution station (loop terminus); the gas-source connector to Beihai First Station and the three intermediate stations (#1 valve chamber, Tieshan Port first station, Nanzhuwan distribution station) should be treated as required waypoints/branch points on any drawn route, not skipped as a straight line between the two anchors. Large-diameter (DN800/DN500 per pilot digest), high-pressure (10/6.3 MPa) branch trunk.
P7664.researcher_notes: Re-verified hnocse.com, yanshougs.com and the dnr.gxzf.gov.cn Wayback snapshot live this pass (all 200 via url_verifier). hnocse.com is the single best source found for this row: a safety-evaluation-industry registry entry that names the project and gives the exact two-segment route description with all station names (quoted in corridor_notes). Could not geocode the Sinopec LNG terminal, Beihai First Station, #1 valve chamber, Tieshan Port first station, or Nanzhuwan distribution station individually — none appear in OSM/Overpass under these names within the Tieshan Port District bounding box, so the LNG terminal start anchor falls back to the district centroid (coarser than the confirmed town-level fix for Xinggang). No GIS/vector layer found. Per the pilot digest's own cross-check: a separately-reported 'Tieshan East Port gas branch pipeline project' (铁山东港天然气支线管道项目, Feb-2024 equity-acquisition report) that the prior pass flagged as a possible undiscovered THIRD Beihai-area pipeline appears, on this pass's reading of P7665's sourcing, to actually just BE P7665 (Donggang Industrial Park branch) under an alternate name — same operator chain (广投管网公司/天圜能源(广西)有限公司 both named in P7665's own commissioning article) — so that lead is resolved, not a new discovery candidate.
P7664.blockers: Sinopec LNG terminal and the three named intermediate stations (#1阀室, 铁山港首站, 南珠湾分输站) could not be individually geocoded — none found in OSM/Overpass by name within the district. Diameter breakdown (800/500/400mm — third value unconfirmed) and SegmentCost discrepancy flagged by the pilot digest remain open and are outside this route-creation task's scope.

P7665.corridor_notes: 12.6km branch ('东港支线') from PipeChina's national-trunk Baisha gas transmission station (国家管网白沙输气站, Baisha Town, Hepu County) to Langgen distribution station (榄根分输站) inside the Tieshan Donggang Industrial Park (铁山东港产业园), on the Hepu County/Tieshan Port District boundary. Design pressure 4 MPa. Built/operated by Guangxi Beihai Guangtou Gas Co. (广西北海广投燃气有限公司) with 广投管网公司 (Guangxi Investment Group's pipeline-network subsidiary). Gas-in/pressure test completed 2024-03-29 (18:35 gas from Baisha reached Langgen; pressure test to 3.8MPa completed 2024-03-29 14:06); official commissioning with first industrial customers (新福兴, 长利 — both glass manufacturers) 2024-08-19.
P7665.researcher_notes: Re-verified gxbhlg.com and gigeps.com live this pass (both 200). gxbhlg.com (the project co-developer's own news page) is a strong single-source route description naming both stations and the exact 12.6km length directly. nengyuanquan.com (the pilot digest's second corroborating source, syndicating the same story with commissioning-date detail) failed url_verifier this pass (ConnectTimeout) and the Wayback API was rate-limited (429) on repeated attempts, so it is NOT included as a ref here even though the pilot digest read it successfully — flagging as a re-check item. gigeps.com/61178 (2025-06-27 feasibility-study procurement notice for a FOLLOW-ON project in the same industrial park) corroborates the area's active buildout but does not itself name P7665's two endpoint stations. Pilot digest already checked P7665 against the roster (incl. P7664) for duplicates and found none (different route, different status, different diameter class) — reconfirmed on this pass; not a duplicate.
